message.content:
Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed to have as few implementation dependencies as possible. It was originally developed by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released in 1995. Key features include:

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Platform independence** | “Write once, run anywhere” – compiled bytecode runs on any device equipped with a Java Virtual Machine (JVM), regardless of underlying hardware or operating system. |
| **Object‑Oriented** | Everything revolves around classes and objects; supports encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction. |
| **Strongly typed & safe** | Compile‑time type checking reduces runtime errors; automatic memory management via garbage collection protects against many common bugs like dangling pointers. |
| **Rich Standard Library** | Extensive APIs covering collections, concurrency, networking, I/O, GUI (Swing/JavaFX), database connectivity ( JDBC ), XML parsing, security, etc. |
| **Multithreading support** | Built‑in thread primitives (`Thread`, `Runnable`) plus higher‑level utilities (`ExecutorService`, concurrent collections). |
| **Enterprise focus** | Widely used in enterprise applications through frameworks such as Spring, Hibernate, Jakarta EE, and more. |

Typical use cases:
* Web servers / application servers  
* Android mobile apps (via Kotlin/Java interop)  
* Desktop GUIs  
* Scientific computing, big data processing (e.g., Hadoop ecosystem)  
* Embedded systems  

Java’s design emphasizes readability, maintainability, and portability—making it one of the most popular languages worldwide.
